reviewKind: independent code-binding review: design-lock v4 correction candidate02 and optional --implementation architecture source preflight
comparisonBaseline: m1-binding4-subject-01 (reviewed ACCEPT-UNIT by m1-binding4-review-01). Its verify_design.py (e6766b6d...), test_design_binding.py (cceb9eb4...) and design-lock.json (90e0533f...) equal the live /Users/sb/code/opensip-ai/opensip product files.
scope: Only the four subject files. Covered: the successor_chain changes (the v4 JSON-content line-selector guard, the malformed candidate-path guard and the documented lexicographic order), the new generation_sources preflight and its dispatch in verify()/main(), the 18 added tests and the unchanged v4 lock. The review makes no product integration, runtime authorization, product or release qualification, or M1 completion claim. It does not accept adapter/closure/drift checks, and it approves no new inventory or contract unit.
acceptanceStatement: Candidate02 is a strictly additive correction over accepted candidate01. The lock is byte-identical, and the test diff removes no lines: the prior 38 tests are unchanged, with 12 binding-history and 6 source-binding tests added (56 in total). In v4, a line selector is refused whenever the parent's pinned bytes decode as JSON under the verifier's decoder, whatever the file suffix. So a line selector and a JSON Pointer can no longer alias one JSON value, including across units and on the real inventory3 bootstrap.rs description (R13 now refuses). Text parents keep line selectors: the real metadata-v2 .md overrides at lines 885 and 325 still verify, and v1-v3 locks keep their prior selector behavior. A malformed inventory candidate path now raises a controlled DesignError, and the lexicographic inheritance order is documented in UNIT.md and in code. The multi-hop semantics reviewed in review01 are unchanged and were independently re-exercised with three-hop reindexing, collapse, conflicts, suppression, stale/extra/null entries, cycles, branches and reuse. The optional --implementation preflight runs only after the full design verification passes and reads only. It requires every mapped architecture pin to equal, by path, sha256 and bytes, an accepted overlay row or an accepted contract candidate. It re-hashes the architecture bytes, requires the implementation copy to be byte-identical through a non-symlink, non-escaping path, and matches the registry digest exactly. Owner fields must agree between map and registry, the schema $id must equal the registry schemaId, and map/registry coverage must be equal. A local repin cannot select unaccepted, superseded or locally modified architecture bytes. On the real architecture checkout with m1-generator-adapter-subject-03 it verifies all 28 sources: 5 lock inputs, 3 metadata-v2 contract candidates and 20 other accepted-overlay rows. The output equals the root source-preflight.json, with executedGeneratorCode=false and productQualification=false. No architecture or adapter file changed.

advisories.topic: Source preflight accepts any accepted overlay row, not only lock inputs, and binds bytes rather than passage-override meaning
advisories.detail: generation_sources joins against effective (the ~12,935-row source+application overlay) plus the contract inputs, not against lock['inputs'] (46). Real data shows 20 of the 28 mapped sources are overlay-only rows. A local map can therefore select any accepted file: S19 selects an unrelated accepted security catalog schema, which verifies. If both map and registry omit schemaId and the architecture document has no $id, the ID check degenerates to None == None. S18 maps the base repository-file-inventory.v1.json, a non-schema file and a passage-override parent whose accepted meaning differs from its bytes, and it verifies. No real mapped source is a passage-override parent, and all 28 real rows carry a non-null schemaId/$id, so this is not a present defect. The UNIT.md claim ('cannot select unaccepted architecture bytes') is accurate. Before relying on the preflight for selection meaning, consider requiring a nonempty schemaId/$id and refusing override parents, or restricting sources to lock inputs plus contract candidates.

advisories.topic: declaredMajor/profile/semanticValidatorOwner are local consistency checks only; rows and paths are open
advisories.detail: The UNIT.md phrase 'source-map coverage/owner fields' means map-vs-registry equality. Changing declaredMajor, profile and owner consistently in both files verifies (S15), and nothing ties these fields to architecture content. Mapping and registry rows are not closed (S17: unknown keys accepted; registry 'recipes' is unchecked). Two implementation paths may map one architecture source (S20), and implementationPath is not confined to schemas/ (S21). Equality comparisons use Python ==, so the CB-A05 1 == 1.0 == True note also applies to declaredMajor. These are adapter/closure concerns that the unit explicitly leaves to separate checks.

advisories.topic: Six source-preflight guards and one dispatch are not isolated by the subject tests
advisories.detail: Mutation run (mutate.py; mutation-results-tests-only.json and mutation-results.json). These mutants survive all 56 tests but are killed by the independent probes: N05 (the accepted join ignores digest/bytes, so a repin at an accepted path after a local architecture change passes; S02, S05); N09 (map/registry owner fields not compared; S14); N14 (duplicate registry path; S13); N15 (contract candidates not added to the preflight selection; killed by the real S01 and S26); N16 (source map top level not closed; S16, S23); N19 (v3 singular contractSuccessor ignored; S26). Current behavior is correct in every case. The tests do kill N01-N04, N06-N08, N10-N13, N17 and N18. Add isolated tests, especially for N05 (accepted path + different digest), because the architecture working tree has uncommitted changes.

The guard uses the verifier's decode. A JSON document with duplicate keys fails decode with DesignError, a ValueError, and is treated as text, so a line selector verifies (V21). That is not an alias, because no JSON Pointer can address such a document either (V22 refuses with 'duplicate JSON key'). A UTF-8 BOM JSON document decodes as JSON, so line refuses and pointer works (V23/V24). A JSON scalar in a .txt file refuses line selectors (V20), and a .json file with non-JSON content keeps them (V19). All outcomes are consistent with 'parses as JSON'. Documenting the duplicate-key case would avoid surprise.

advisories.topic: Uncontrolled exception types remain on malformed data
advisories.detail: Mapping an accepted non-JSON architecture file (an .md) raises json.JSONDecodeError, not DesignError (S22). A contract override parent whose path is a list still raises TypeError in the unchanged contract_successor (V39; carried CB-A06). main() catches ValueError, KeyError and TypeError, so the CLI still exits 1 without passing (S34 checks exit codes), but API callers see non-DesignError types. The inventory candidate-path case from B4-A04 is fixed (V36/V37, prior C27).

advisories.topic: The implementation root's own lock/tool is not bound to --lock
advisories.detail: The preflight uses the --lock design lock (by default next to the running verifier) and never reads ROOT/design-lock.json or ROOT/tools/verify_design.py. Adapter subject-03 carries the older v3 lock (d80a7eee...) and verifier (19bb3318...), and the run still verifies against the subject v4 lock (S33). This matches the stated trust model ('callers start from the reviewed developer checkout'; not self-attestation or an execution guard), and the v3 lock also selects the same 28 sources (S26). Running a reviewed verifier against a different implementation checkout proves only that the source bytes are accepted, not that the checkout carries that lock.

B4-A01 is resolved: the tests now kill M02, M03, M07, M09, M10, M11 and M15; 22 of 24 prior mutants are killed by the tests, confirming the claim. B4-A02 is resolved for v4 by the JSON-content guard (C25/R13 now refuse; the v3 compatibility test passes). B4-A03 is resolved by documentation in UNIT.md and a code comment. The candidate-path half of B4-A04 is resolved; its IndexError note is unchanged, since that code is unchanged. B4-A05 still applies: M08 and M22 are equivalent and survive tests and probes. B4-A06 still applies: CB-A02, CB-A04, CB-A05 and CB-A06 remain, because selected_passage, contract_successor and same_reference are byte-identical. Re-running review01's probe.py on candidate02 gives 43 of 46; the three changes (C12, C25, C27) are exactly the intended stricter or controlled refusals.

positiveEvidence: Subject integrity: the sibling manifest sha256 was e8043832... before and after. All 4 files matched sha256 and bytes before and after, and the file set is exact. The subject was copied to subject-copy/ before any output; diff -r shows the copy identical to the subject at the end, with no __pycache__ or .pyc in either.

Diff against candidate01: design-lock.json is byte-identical. verify_design.py adds the candidate-path guard, the v4 JSON-content line guard, the order comment, generation_sources, the implementation parameter/dispatch and the --implementation flag. Every other line is unchanged. The test diff has 0 removed lines. UNIT.md was rewritten to describe the correction and the preflight.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests in subject-copy (Python 3.14.6): Ran 56 tests OK.

Real CLI: the subject verifier + subject lock + --architecture /Users/sb/code/opensip-ai/opensip_arch + --implementation m1-generator-adapter-subject-03 exits 0. It reports passed=true, inputsVerified=46, inventory3 (4 added files), the metadata-v2 unit (9 inputs, 4 overrides), empty inheritance and generationSources {sourcesVerified: 28, executedGeneratorCode: false, productQualification: false}. The output is JSON-equal to root m1-binding4-root-validation-02/source-preflight.json, and without --implementation all other fields are identical (out/).

Root real-mirror probes (root-rerun/real_probe.py, paths pointed at subject-copy): 14 of 14 met, including R13 (line/pointer alias on real inventory3 now refuses) and the two-hop real mirror R05-R07 (bootstrap.rs index 7 to 8).

Independent synthetic v4 probes (probe_v4.py, probe-v4-results.json): 42 of 42 met. They cover v1-v3 compatibility (v2 without a contract unit; a v3 JSON line selector passes while the same selector in v4 refuses; a text line in v4 passes). They cover three-hop reindexing to the final index, stale intermediate indexes, an intermediate-parent entry, identical ancestors collapsing, conflicting ancestors, a conflicting or identical direct final override, extra-key and null inheritance entries, lexicographic order across 12 rows and non-final hop inheritance. On aliasing they cover JSON detection by content, not suffix, in both directions; JSON contract members; duplicate-key and BOM edge cases; leading-zero and escape pointer aliases; and mixed selectors. On reuse: inventory candidate path, overlay-only path, earlier unit record, forward parent, branch and cycle. On malformed data: non-object chain entries, noncanonical and list candidates, null contract entries, list override parent paths, a missing inheritance field and version 4.0.

Independent source-preflight probes (probe_sources.py, probe-sources-results.json): 35 of 35 met, on the real architecture (read only), a temporary pinned-file mirror and temporary copies of the adapter schemas/. The following refuse: accepted path with changed bytes plus a full local repin; unchanged pin with changed bytes on disk; an unaccepted on-disk trial schema; a superseded source-manifest row; the metadata-v1 previousCandidate; a one-byte copy difference; a file symlink to the architecture; a directory symlink escaping the root; a symlinked source-map.json; registry-only and map-only rows; a duplicate registry path; owner field mismatch; extra map top-level key; schemaVersion true or 1.0; an uppercase digest; a consistent $id change; a list row; an extra pin key; a missing root; and an invalid design lock (the design error is reported first). These verify: the accepted v3 adapter lock with 28 sources; the v2 derivation refuses envelope4. CLI exit codes are 0 and 1. The 92 watched architecture files and 87 adapter files were unchanged before and after.
Mutation run: 43 mutants (24 prior, 19 new). The 56 tests kill 35. Tests plus probes kill all 41 non-equivalent mutants, and only M08 and M22, both equivalent, survive.
negativeEvidence: Behaviors that verify and that the review records as advisories, not defects: an arbitrary accepted overlay schema (S19) or a non-schema passage-override parent without schemaId/$id (S18) can be a generation source; owner/major/profile are only consistency-checked (S15); rows are open (S17); duplicate architecture mapping (S20) and paths outside schemas/ (S21) are allowed; the implementation root's own lock is ignored (S33).
Uncontrolled exception types: JSONDecodeError on a non-JSON source (S22) and TypeError on a list override parent path (V39). The CLI still fails closed.
Test isolation gaps: N05, N09, N14, N15, N16 and N19 survive the 56 tests.

An initial V29 probe fixture overwrote a pinned base input, so it refused on digest before reaching the reuse guard. It was corrected to use an accepted overlay-only path and then met its expectation. This was a probe defect, not a subject defect.
limitations: Code-binding review of a developer preflight only. It does not establish product integration, product or release qualification, runtime authorization, OS execution confinement, remote attestation or cryptographic reviewer identity; the checked-in lock and reviewed checkout remain the trust anchor.

It does not review or accept the adapter subject-03 source map/registry content, generator closure/options/outputs or drift checks. The 28-source run shows only that those bytes are accepted design bytes and consistent with the local registry.

The base source/application approval and the substance of inventory3, metadata-v2 and the mapped schemas were not reaudited. Multi-hop inheritance with non-empty inheritance still exists only in synthetic fixtures and real-byte mirrors; no real second inventory hop exists.
The architecture working tree has unrelated uncommitted changes. Verification depends on exact pins, not git state, and no git commands that write were run.
The older v1-v3 guards (selected_passage, contract_successor, inventory_successor) were not re-mutated; carried advisories CB-A02/A04/A05/A06/A07 still apply.

Artifacts in this directory: subject-copy/, before-hashes.txt, after-hashes.txt, out/, prior/ (review01 probe re-run), root-rerun/ (root real-probe re-run), probe_v4.py, probe_sources.py, mutate.py and their result JSON files. Temporary fixtures and mirrors were deleted.
